_comment: Fragment 28 — D-71, six stale claims corrected; G65 tier-sweep blind spot, G66 uncovered settings file, G25 closed properly. Merged 2026-08-21.

nodes.label: D-71 — Six Stale Claims Corrected
nodes.description: Six claims across four documents had stopped being true: the CI row and lockfile count and header status in the artifact inventory, three assertions in the build spec that no test runner or CI existed, section 5.1's list of outstanding Chief Editor decisions, and Modular_PRD section 10's Q2 row. All six were corrected in place, and the section 5.1 tally was removed rather than restated.
nodes.rationale: The most consequential was section 5.1's opening line, which a decision-maker reads to know what they still owe: it named Q2, QC, G23 and G24 as outstanding when all four were already decided. Only those four were removed — the remaining twelve were not individually re-verified, and that limit is stated rather than implied.

nodes.label: G65 — The Tier Sweep Verifies Arrival, Not Correctness
nodes.description: D-54 propagation is checked by asking whether a decision ID appears in each tier it claims. Presence satisfies the check and staleness is invisible to it. Proven twice: D-70 appeared three times in the artifact inventory while a row still read specified-not-installed, and D-57 appeared four times in Modular_PRD while section 10's Q2 row still read Open. Both passed.
nodes.rationale: All six of D-71's stale claims survived a passing C-14 run, which makes this the parent defect rather than one finding among them. Opened rather than fixed: the remedy is a stricter check comparing a tier claim against that tier's content, which is executable code and covered by the build guardrail. Recorded so the limitation is not mistaken for coverage — any future claim that propagation is verified must say which kind, arrival or correctness.

nodes.label: G66 — A Shared File No Check Covers
nodes.description: The .claude/settings.json file is checked in and shared across all three agents, and no C-14 check covers it — the shared-core hash compares only the three agent rule files. Demonstrated live rather than hypothesised: a hand edit left the file as invalid JSON, and Claude Code silently ignores a settings file it cannot parse, so both hooks were disabled with no error and no warning.
nodes.rationale: This is the D-58 failure mode in a file D-58 never considered — a silent overwrite, undetected. The only symptom was the absence of hook output, which is indistinguishable from a hook that had nothing to say. A JSON parse check across the settings cascade is one line and would have caught it.

nodes.label: G25 Was Closed Against Two of Its Three Targets
nodes.description: G25's own Fix named three targets: CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md and docs/README.md. The two agent files carried five references each to docs/v1/; docs/README.md carried zero. The missing one is the what-governs-what authority map, whose table listed source, governance, journal and this folder with no v1 row at all. D-71 added it and closed the gap against all three.
nodes.rationale: The exact defect G25 describes was still live inside a gap marked Closed for two days. A gap closed against a narrower remedy than the one it specified, with the descope never recorded — which is why the closure text named only the agent files while the Fix named three.

nodes.label: docs/README.md Is an Entry Point, Not a Tier
nodes.description: D-71 first claimed docs/README.md as a D-54 tier in its applicability table. The tier sweep rejected it, and the check was right: the file generates no FR, no AC and no sprint sequence. The v1 row landed there because that is where G25's defect lived, and the closure is traceable through section 5.1 and the decision section rather than through a tier claim.
nodes.rationale: An editing target is not automatically a propagation tier. Recorded because the distinction was only forced by the check rejecting the claim, and because the tempting alternative — citing a gap ID inside a user-facing README to satisfy the check — would have been gaming the control rather than obeying it.
